title: Visiting the sick
hook: whoever visits the sick is in the harvest of the garden until he returns

segments.voice: Yesterday, honoring the elders, and your line: honor the gray hair. Did you catch a sigh before it got out? Today a new stretch of the life cycle begins: illness, and then death. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-five.

On the Day of Rising, in a hadith in Sahih Muslim, Allah speaks to a person, and the words are strange. I was sick, He says, and you did not visit Me. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, tells it. And the person is baffled. My Lord, how could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds? The answer comes back, in paraphrase: did you not know that My servant so-and-so was sick, and you did not visit him? Had you visited him, you would have found Me with him. The bedside, in this story, is not an ordinary room.
screen: `I WAS SICK, AND YOU DID NOT VISIT ME.` → `HOW COULD I VISIT YOU?` → `YOU WOULD HAVE FOUND ME WITH HIM.`

segments.voice: The word is 'iyadah, visiting the sick. The hadith in Muslim keeps going, and it widens. I asked you for food, and you did not feed Me. I asked you for water, and you did not give Me to drink. Each time the same bafflement, and each time the same answer: My servant asked you. Had you done it, you would have found it with Me. A different hadith in Muslim gives the visit its picture. Whoever visits a sick person, the Prophet said, remains in the khurfah of the garden until he returns. Someone asked what the khurfah was. The answer: its harvest, its fruit being gathered. So the walk to the hospital, the time in the plastic chair, the walk back to the car, all of it, in this picture, is time spent picking fruit in Paradise. Al-Bukhari keeps a short command that puts it next to other basic duties, in paraphrase: feed the hungry, visit the sick, and set the captive free. Notice what the visit doesn't require. No cure. No perfect words. You're not asked to fix anything. You're asked to show up, sit near, and go home. Bring nothing but yourself, if that's all you have. The harvest starts at the door.
screen: `'IYADAH: VISITING THE SICK.` · `FOOD, WATER, AND A VISIT.` · `THE KHURFAH: THE GARDEN'S HARVEST.` · `NO CURE NEEDED, JUST COME.`

segments.voice: The practice: visit or call someone ill. Settle, and breathe. Who do you know who is sick right now? Someone in the hospital, someone recovering at home, someone with an illness that doesn't go away and that people have stopped asking about. Let one face come. Now decide how you'll reach them: a visit if you can, a call if you can't, a message if that's all that's possible. Think of your first sentence. Keep it simple. How are you, really? If you pray, you can ask for their healing in your own words. The bell holds the time.
'Iyadah. Visiting the sick: a visit that, in the hadith, keeps you in the garden's harvest until you come home. Today's word.
Your line: the garden's harvest. Today, make the visit or the call you chose, and stay long enough to really ask. Tomorrow, illness as expiation. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Muslims visit the sick at home and in hospital as a sunnah, often bringing food and making a short supplication for the person's healing, citing the hadith that the visitor is in the harvest of the garden until they return.

match.prompt: visiting the sick — tap the pairs.
pairs: and you did not visit Me

myth: in the hadith, the visitor has to bring a cure
the visit itself is the deed; nothing in it asks you to fix anything.
in Muslim, the visitor remains in the garden's harvest until he returns
the khurfah, the fruit being gathered.
in the hadith qudsi, Allah asks only about prayers missed
He asks about the sick not visited, the hungry not fed, the thirsty not given drink.

fork.setup: on the Day of Rising you hear: I was sick, and you did not visit Me. what do you answer?
options: You were never sick, my Lord.
how could I visit You, Lord of the worlds?
fork.reveal: the person is baffled, and is told: My servant was sick; had you visited him, you would have found Me with him.

trapdoor: what you thought: visiting the sick is a kind courtesy.
what it means: in the hadith, the visit keeps you in the garden's harvest, and Allah is found with the sick.
what a scholar hears: the khurfah of the garden in Sahih Muslim, and the hadith qudsi where Allah says, I was sick and you did not visit Me.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 2569 (hadith qudsi: I was sick and you did not visit Me)

notes: Muslim 2568, 2569 and Bukhari 5649 paraphrased; confirm numbers and wording.
